blindSummary:
Same-sex conduct has never been criminalised in this country — but the reality on the ground is severe insecurity: mob justice against perceived LGBT people is documented, police extortion is routine, one region is an active conflict zone (an armed rebel group), and an LGBT organisation based in a large provincial city reports systematic violations in its 2024 submission to the country's UN human-rights review. There is no legal gender recognition and no protection infrastructure; the small queer scene in the capital is underground.

For a visitor: no statutory exposure, but outing risks mob violence with no effective state protection anywhere in the country.
blindOutOfScope: Conflict conditions in the affected region are general; mob justice against LGBT people is documented in UN review submissions.
blindSourceSummaries: A country page on a global LGBTI legal database: documents this country's legal status for same-sex conduct and gender recognition.

Civil-society stakeholder submission to the country's 5th-cycle UN human-rights review (March 2024) by a local LGBT organisation and others: the state does not criminalise same-sex relations but neither protects nor promotes LGBTIQ+ rights; public displays of same-sex affection can be prosecuted under indecent-exposure provisions (a penal-code clause on publicly 'outraging morals by actions').

An international rights group (Dec 2017): reports rebels recruited child fighters to crush opposition protests — general human-rights context for this country's security environment, not LGBT-specific.

An LGBTQ+ travel guide rates this country at its top warning level for LGBTQ+ travellers: no explicit national criminalisation, but the penal code's indecency provision and local ordinances are applied against LGBTQ people; armed militia groups in the conflict-affected region have committed extreme violence against LGBTQ people with near-total impunity; collapse of state authority means legal protections are theoretical.

Encyclopedia-mirror overview of LGBT rights here: same-sex activity legal for both sexes (never outlawed, even under its former administration), equal age of consent; but no gender-identity recognition, no relationship recognition (same-sex marriage banned constitutionally since 2006), limited protections; powerful religious groups promote the view that homosexuality is immoral; public same-sex affection can trigger prosecution under indecency provisions.
A queer travel-information site's country entry: a travel-oriented overview of the legal situation and safety considerations for LGBTQ visitors to this country.
